articles.title: INSTAGRAM'S EFFECT BUILDER MAKES NEW FILTERS FROM AI PROMPTS
articles.summary: Instagram's new Effect Builder, available now on the web to US residents over 18, turns AI prompts into custom Stories filters. Users can attach style reference images, preview effects on their own photos, and refine through follow-up prompts. An AI prompt-rewrite option adds paragraphs of style detail yet barely changes the result, and every effect must pass a safety review before others can use it.

articles.title: ADOBE AND DISNEY TEAM UP TO BUILD AI TOOLS FOR THE NEXT GENERATION OF STORYTELLING
articles.summary: Adobe has become Disney's Official AI Innovation Partner under a multi-year deal focused on storytelling, creativity, and responsible AI use. Adobe will give Disney early access to Firefly, Firefly Foundry, Premiere, and Photoshop, plus its own engineers and researchers. Through Firefly Foundry, Disney's models learn its characters and art styles, and Imagineering R&D already uses them to turn sketches into 2D concept art.

articles.title: GOOGLE MESSAGES HOMEPAGE REDESIGN: PINNED CHAT AVATARS, BOTTOM SEARCH, CORNER GEMINI
articles.summary: Google Messages is testing a redesigned Android homepage that displays pinned conversations as large contact avatars above the regular message list, similar to Apple's iMessage. Search moves from the top of the screen to a floating button near the bottom, alongside a new-chat button that changes shape while scrolling to improve one-handed usability. The Gemini shortcut also moves to the upper-right corner beside the profile image, with the changes currently rolling out selectively to beta testers.

articles.title: WELCOME TO THE BEIGE ERA OF PRODUCT DESIGN. HERE'S YOUR WAY OUT
articles.summary: Digital products are converging on the same look, driven by AI tools that repeat common solutions, vibe-design tools, shared UI libraries like shadcn/ui, and optimization culture. Convergence is "the floor," so designers should standardize what users expect. Borrowing automotive design's idea of "jewelry," teams should protect a few distinctive details, such as emotional moments like a first payment or a signed contract.

articles.title: MAKING IMMERSIVE LLM CHAT EXPERIENCES MORE ACCESSIBLE
articles.summary: Chat interfaces like Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini are interactive web content, so WCAG applies to them like any other page. A single live region announcing replies after streaming ends, hidden per-message headings, and sparing landmark use keep screen reader navigation workable. Skip links, Control+F6 shortcuts, user preferences, and research with disabled participants round out the approach.

articles.title: WHEN TOUCH MAKES SENSE ON A LAPTOP
articles.summary: Touchscreen laptops can make certain interactions faster than using a trackpad, particularly when selecting large targets or performing brief, direct actions. In a single-participant experiment across six tasks, touch averaged 1.39 seconds compared with 1.74 seconds for the trackpad, while previous research found similar advantages for some interactions. Touch remains less accurate for small targets and can cause fatigue during extended use, making it better suited as a complementary input method rather than a replacement for traditional laptop controls.

articles.summary: Emil Kowalski's collection of 17 AI agent skills helps developers build and refine interfaces through specialized guidance for animation, gestures, mobile interactions, prototyping, performance, accessibility-related edge cases, and design engineering.

articles.title: "X IS DEAD" IS DEAD
articles.summary: Figma, wireframing, design files, and design systems aren't disappearing, but the standardized toolchains that once defined product design are fragmenting into increasingly personalized workflows. Designers now move between sketching tools, AI prompts, coding agents, and other applications, making it harder for organizations to enforce consistency through shared software alone. Design systems must therefore become tool-independent infrastructure that communicates not just components and tokens but also product principles, decision-making context, and the intentions behind design choices.

articles.title: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN VISUAL DESIGN AND USER EXPERIENCE DESIGN
articles.summary: Visual design is only one part of UX, usually among the last decisions made, and it depends on an interdisciplinary team. Jesse James Garrett's five planes run from strategy through scope, structure, and skeleton to surface, where visual design sits. Continuous testing feeds back into decisions at every level.
